top.title: Anthropic prices its IPO at $83 a share, valuing it near $1.5 trillion
top.summary: Anthropic sold about 980 million shares at $83, above its $70-78 range, raising $81.3 billion in the largest IPO on record. It starts trading on Nasdaq today as ANT, with Amazon and Google together owning close to 30%.
top.why: Claude is now a public-company vendor with quarterly disclosures, which helps when Legal, Procurement or IT ask about vendor stability for the Claude workflows you run.

top.title: How the Claude Code team makes agents verify their own work
top.summary: Anthropic describes how Claude writes and reviews most of Claude Code: every agent gets automated checks it must pass, it can retry a failing check up to three times before handing off to a human, and it is never allowed to change the checks that judge it.
top.why: The same pattern fits PMM skills: give each workflow a fixed rubric (messaging pillars, banned claims, required sources) that the agent runs against itself, with a retry cap and a human escalation step.

top.title: Citi makes customers liable for what their AI agents do
top.summary: Citi changed its terms so customers carry responsibility for actions third-party AI tools take on their accounts, even after a hack, and other banks are moving the same way.
top.why: A clear signal that accountability for agent actions sits with whoever connects the agent, which belongs in the guardrail doc for any marketing agent that can post, send or spend.

try_this.title: A self-check prompt for any PMM workflow
try_this.how: Add to one existing skill: 'Before drafting, tell me how you'll check this against [rubric]. After drafting, run the check and report results. If it fails, fix it up to three times, then stop and tell me. Don't change the rubric, and flag anything you couldn't check.' Compare how many edits you make versus last week.

workflows.title: Slack adds agents to no-code workflows, with approval before posting
workflows.summary: Slack workflows can now include Slackbot or custom agents as steps, such as a weekly agent that ranks open deals, and output waits for a person to approve it before it posts.
workflows.why: A low-effort way to run a scheduled CI or launch-status summary inside the channel where sales already works, with review built in.

workflows.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for Sales with Salesforce and HubSpot data
workflows.summary: A new plugin plus 30-plus integrations pull CRM and customer data into ChatGPT so sellers can research accounts and prep deals in one place.
workflows.why: If Camunda sellers adopt it, battlecards and messaging need to be reachable from inside ChatGPT, not only in the enablement portal.

governance.title: FTC's AI enforcement now reaches B2B suppliers of marketing claims
governance.summary: In its third year, the FTC's Operation AI Comply is going after companies that supply misleading AI marketing materials to resellers and partners, not only the sellers themselves.
governance.why: Partner kits and co-marketing copy about agentic capabilities now carry their own risk, so AI claims in those assets need the same substantiation check as direct campaigns.

governance.title: GAO jailbroke four major chatbots into producing attack plans
governance.summary: The federal watchdog used common bypass techniques to get ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok to produce workable attack plans within 12 hours, though the tests used spring 2026 model versions.
governance.why: Useful context for Security conversations: vendor safeguards are a baseline, not a guarantee, so internal guardrails and review steps still matter.

competitive.title: Mondelez and Accenture apply AI to order-to-cash
competitive.summary: Mondelez is using AI with Accenture to cut manual handoffs between customer service, fulfillment and collections across millions of transactions a year.
competitive.why: A named enterprise example of AI applied to an end-to-end process with many system handoffs, the exact story Camunda tells about orchestration; worth tracking which platform sits underneath.

competitive.title: Agents raise individual output, not team alignment
competitive.summary: A short essay argues that agents make each person more productive but do nothing for coordination across people, which becomes the new bottleneck.
competitive.why: Supports the orchestration argument: the value shifts from single agents to how work moves between agents, people and systems.

enablement.title: Hesitation, not skill, holds people back from delegating to AI
enablement.summary: A Rundown educator who trains teams says people avoid handing tedious work to AI for the same reason they avoid handing it to coworkers, and suggests pointing a browser agent at the internal tool everyone dreads.
enablement.why: A concrete enablement exercise: ask each marketer to name one clunky internal system and run a browser-agent task on it during training.

landscape.title: Google's Gemini 4 Neon undercuts Opus 5.5 on price
landscape.summary: Google's fourth Gemini 4 model in two months is a mid-tier release that tops Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol on most of Google's own benchmarks, especially long-document and office work, at $3/$15 per million tokens.
landscape.why: Another strong, cheaper option for high-volume document tasks like content audits, if your stack can route between models.
